script.stored_text_completeness: All 20600 canonical characters read sequentially in full in 2 bounded ranges; auto-generated untimed text; stored ending is complete ("financially subscribed to everyone else's wealth."); many fillers ("Um", "Uh"); ASR ("I ate 3 years", "Fair and Canvas", "Now now"); audio, timed delivery and editing unverified.
script.opening_words: You check your bank account and feel confused. You make decent money. You're not buying ridiculous stuff. You're being responsible. Yet somehow you have exactly $47 left until Friday and it's only Tuesday. Sound familiar? Here's what's actually happening to your money. You're being slowly bled to death $15 at a time by the subscription economy that's designed to make you perpetually broke. My name is Nick and I spend way too much time thinking about why people who make
script.ending_words: built. Every monthly payment you eliminate is money you can invest in assets that actually belong to you. The companies getting rich from your subscriptions understand this perfectly. That's why they own everything while convincing you to rent it. Stop being a permanent renter of your own life. Start owning things again. Your future self will thank you when you're financially free, instead of financially subscribed to everyone else's wealth.
script.analysis: Full 20600 canonical characters read. A rant-style essay: "$47 until Friday" hook; ownership vs rental economy; subscription study ($86 vs $273); streaming overload; gym memberships; car payments as transport subscriptions; monthly framing; software subscriptions (Adobe, Microsoft, business tools); phone plans; insurance and coffee subscriptions; lost ownership skills; company valuations (Netflix, Adobe); digital feudalism; subscription vs ownership mentality; data and dependence; opportunity cost ($1,100 at 7% = $1.3M); expanding subscription categories; action steps. Directly verified: C+R study says $219, not $273. Reproduces: $67,200 car, $3,600 Adobe, $1.34M. Stale/doubtful: market caps, Fair/Canvas, savings comparison. Heavy fillers. The stored ending is complete.
